content.title: About
content.content: Coffee flavored liqueur is a sweet alcoholic beverage made from spirit, sugar and natural coffee flavorings. It offers a rich coffee taste with a gentle sweetness, aromatic bouquet and smooth texture. Typically served as a digestif or used in cocktails.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The coffee aroma is achieved by adding extracts from roasted coffee beans.
The first coffee liqueur appeared in Europe in the 19th century as a way to preserve coffee flavor.
Liqueur is often used in cuisine: to soak cakes, ice cream and sauces.
Alcohol content usually ranges from 15 % to 25 % ABV.
In some countries coffee liqueur is a traditional holiday gift.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Moderate alcohol consumption can promote relaxation and improve mood.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Coffee aroma stimulates gastric juice secretion, which can aid digestion.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Excessive intake can lead to alcohol poisoning, liver issues and dependence.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels may be unsuitable for people with diabetes or those watching weight.

items.title: Coffee allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coffee components.

content.title: How to Enjoy
content.content: The liqueur can be enjoyed neat, on the rocks, or in cocktails. It pairs well with desserts, ice cream, chocolate and fruit salads. For cocktails use 30–50 ml of the liqueur depending on desired strength.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dark place with the cap tightly sealed. At temperatures above 20 °C the aroma may gradually fade. Once opened, it is best consumed within 12 months.
